newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais posts increased profit.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais posts increased profit.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais, the French bank which nearly collapsed under the weight of its lending excesses, on Thursday reported an increased 1996 profit.

The state-controlled bank, which the government plans to recapitalise and privatise by early 1999, said in a statement that net attributable profit rose to 202 million francs ($35.5 million) from a profit in 1995 of 13 million francs.
The figures included charges of 2.48 billion francs for restructuring and 200 million francs to prepare for the move to European monetary union in 1999.

"We are rather optimistic about an improvement in our pre-tax, pre-exceptional result in 1997," Peyrelevade said, adding he expected "modest growth" in banking income, a firm hand on general expenses and lower risk costs compared to 1996.
To that will be added the effects of the 1996 restructuring.
He said that the first two months of the year had been according to plan.
